args.rationale: Emergency transfer to the operating room is needed for surgical treatment. The patient has MRSA bacteremia with infective endocarditis (hpi_003) and developed rapid hemodynamic deterioration with cardiogenic shock (physical_exam_005). Echo showed new LV wall-motion abnormalities and a pericardial effusion that progressed to tamponade (ecg_008). Emergency pericardiocentesis drained yellowish, turbid fluid (procedure_result_011). Coronary angiography then showed a disrupted prior stent and a rapidly enlarging coronary pseudoaneurysm (imaging_009), and DIC was reported (lab_007). A rapidly enlarging mycotic coronary pseudoaneurysm with an infected, disrupted stent is at risk of rupture and cannot be treated safely without surgery. Surgery has been ordered (order recorded; outcome not available in source).
args.followup_or_handoff: Direct handoff to cardiothoracic surgery and cardiac anesthesia for emergent excision of the infected stent and pseudoaneurysm, debridement, coronary bypass as needed and pericardial washout and drainage. Continue IV anti-MRSA therapy under infectious diseases guidance. Send operative tissue and pericardial fluid for Gram stain, culture and pathology, and repeat blood cultures. Manage DIC with the hematology team and blood bank (guided blood-product replacement, crossmatch). Use vasopressor or inotropic support and invasive monitoring as needed. Transfer to cardiac ICU after surgery, with intraoperative or postoperative TEE to assess valves and look for abscess. Plan prolonged IV antibiotics with follow-up cultures and echocardiography.
